source_refs.note: Exercise 6.6, Question 1 (book p. 215-215); answer key PDF 308-309; checked with sympy

blocks.prompt: 1. A comet has a parabolic orbit with the sun at the focus. When the comet is 100 million km from the sun, the line joining the sun and the comet makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the axis of the parabola. How close will the comet get to the sun?
blocks.explanation:
This is Example 29 again with numbers: a parabolic orbit with the sun at the focus.
Given: the comet is 100 (million km) from the focus and the line makes \(60^\circ\) with the axis. To find: the nearest distance, which is the focus-to-vertex distance \(a\).
Plan: write the comet's coordinates with a right triangle, substitute in \(y^2 = 4ax\), solve for \(a\).
steps:
Given: parabolic orbit, sun at the focus; comet 100 million km from the sun; the sun-comet line makes \(60^\circ\) with the axis.
To find: the least distance between the comet and the sun.
Method: as in Example 29, take the orbit \(y^2 = 4ax\) with the sun at the focus \(S(a, 0)\). The vertex is the point of a parabola nearest to its focus, so the answer is \(|OS| = a\). We work in millions of km.

Coordinates of the comet (comet beyond the sun, as in Figure 6.30)
Let \(P(x, y)\) be the comet and \(Q\) the foot of the perpendicular from \(P\) to the axis.
\[x - a = 100\cos 60^\circ = 50\]
\[y = 100\sin 60^\circ = 50\sqrt{3}\]
So \(P = (a + 50,\ 50\sqrt{3})\).
Why: in the right triangle \(SQP\) the hypotenuse is \(SP = 100\); \(SQ\) lies along the axis and \(PQ\) is perpendicular to it.

Substitute in \(y^2 = 4ax\)
\[(50\sqrt{3})^2 = 4a(a + 50)\]
\[7500 = 4a^2 + 200a\]
\[a^2 + 50a - 1875 = 0\]
Why: \(P\) is on the orbit, so its coordinates satisfy the equation. We divided by 4.

Solve the quadratic
\[(a + 75)(a - 25) = 0\]
\[a = 25 \text{ or } a = -75\]
Why: \(75 \times 25 = 1875\) and \(75 - 25 = 50\). A distance is positive, so \(a = 25\).

Quick check with the focal distance
\[SP = x + a = (a + 50) + a\]
\[100 = 2a + 50\]
\[a = 25 \;\checkmark\]
Why: for \(y^2 = 4ax\) the distance of a point from the focus equals its distance \(x + a\) from the directrix \(x = -a\).

The other possible position
The axis is a straight line, so \(SP\) can also make \(60^\circ\) with it on the vertex side of the sun. Then \(Q\) lies between \(O\) and \(S\):
\[x - a = -50\]
\[7500 = 4a(a - 50)\]
\[a^2 - 50a - 1875 = 0\]
\[(a - 75)(a + 25) = 0\]
\[a = 75\]
Why: same triangle, but \(Q\) is now on the other side of \(S\). Check: \(x = 75 - 50 = 25 > 0\) and \(SP = x + a = 25 + 75 = 100\) \(\checkmark\).
blocks.final_answer: 25 million km (comet beyond the sun, the set-up of Example 29 and Figure 6.30). If the comet is on the vertex side of the sun, the least distance is 75 million km.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints 75 million km. The question does not say on which side of the sun the comet is. With the set-up of the book's own Example 29 (Figure 6.30, the comet beyond the sun) the answer is 25 million km; 75 million km is correct only when the comet is on the vertex side of the sun.
